justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: PT for TMD shows consistent pain and function improvement; specialty certification vs general PT comparison absent.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Course-based certification; variable length; moderate cost and time investment.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Applicable to TMD and craniomandibular dysfunction patients; limited scope in general PT settings.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: TMD PT billed under standard codes; some dental-medical crossover billing; no TMJ cert-specific premium.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Moderate demand in craniomandibular and facial pain specialty settings.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: TMD patients with chronic jaw pain value specialized treatment.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: TMJ patients are often desperate, underserved by medicine/dentistry, and willing to pay cash for relief.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Few clinicians take TMJ cases, and dentist referral channels support premium per-visit rates.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Real scarcity; most outpatient PTs don't treat TMJ, making this a defensible niche.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Other PTs can be trained, but the niche depth makes scaling moderate at best.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Awareness is growing, particularly via dental and orofacial pain communities.
justifications.business.efficiency: Several reasonable pathways (PTBCA, Rocabado, etc.) at moderate cost and time.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Not a tenure-relevant credential; viewed as CE rather than scholarly standing.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Modest publication activity; orofacial pain research exists but is more dental/medical than PT-led.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Adds depth to head/neck or orthopedic curricula but is rarely a core teaching topic.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Mixed; manual therapy and exercise for TMD has support, but heterogeneity and small trials dominate.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Almost never appears in faculty job postings.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Reasonable cost/time, but limited academic return on that investment.
